sections.body: The AI Lawyer covers how artificial intelligence is used in legal work across ten areas. In discovery, systems sort and classify large document sets, flag privilege, and surface relevant material for review. In contracts, tools compare clauses, draft from templates, and track obligations across a lifecycle. Legal research tools retrieve cases and statutes, summarize holdings, and suggest arguments, while governance teams use AI to monitor regulatory changes and internal policies. Litigation analytics models estimate outcomes and judge tendencies from historical data, and firm operations use AI for billing, staffing, and security. The field is not about robots arguing in court, it is about software changing how legal teams read, write, search, and decide.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some tasks are genuinely useful now, especially document classification, contract review, and legal search, where AI can reduce repetitive reading. Other tasks remain contested, including outcome prediction and autonomous legal advice, because models can reflect bias, miss context, and produce confident errors. The public record shows the pressure: this site tracks 146 active AI lawsuits, 92 of them intellectual property, and 29 AI case law precedents. Regulation is moving quickly, with 215 compliance and regulation pages and 6940 state AI bills tracked here. What is solved is narrow, repeatable extraction and retrieval, what is not solved is judgment, accountability, and the boundary between assistance and unauthorized practice. Honest limits include data quality, confidentiality, explainability, and the fact that legal standards vary by jurisdiction.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages under this section divide the work into ten connected views. E-Discovery and Large-Scale Document Analysis covers review pipelines and privilege, while Contract Lifecycle and Algorithmic Drafting follows agreements from template to renewal. Legal Research and Case Strategy looks at retrieval and argument support, and Corporate Governance and Regulatory Compliance tracks board duties and policy monitoring. Intellectual Property and Trademark Strategy sits beside Litigation Prediction and Judicial Analytics, one for rights and one for forecasts. Legal Operations, Infrastructure and Security, Data Privacy and Cyber-Regulatory Compliance, Emerging Legal Frameworks, and AI Security Audits and Enterprise Enablement cover the back office, the privacy rules, the new statutes, and the audits that let firms adopt these tools. A reader would go to each for a different layer of the same problem, from a single document review to the law being written around it.
